Spectral methods provide a principled way to compress redundant feature sets by focusing on dominant eigenspaces, thereby mitigating the curse of dimensionality. State-transition models address this by explicitly modeling temporal dependencies and strategic feedback loops, but require substantial data to estimate accurate transition matrices. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Opposing agents (e.g., bookmakers vs. bettors) operate under bounded rationality, leading to systematic biases in price formation. A sophisticated model must anticipate these heuristics while remaining agnostic about their exact cognitive mechanisms. For instance, if bookmakers apply momentum-based adjustments, the model should detect and counteract this trend without assuming explicit knowledge of their algorithms. Conversely, if bettors exhibit herding behavior, the model must identify rare deviations that signal mispricing opportunities.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity conditions require that the feature covariance matrix remains well-conditioned across different data splits. Leakage occurs when future information (e.g., injury updates after game start) inadvertently influences past predictions, yielding spuriously high accuracy metrics. To prevent this, temporal exclusions must be enforced during cross-validation, ensuring that held-out sets contain only strictly historical data. Additionally, the model's input space must not contain variables derived from the target variable itself, as this creates circular reasoning that undermines generalizability.
